summary: The Mail Ballot Integrity Act prohibits states from sending unsolicited mail ballots for federal elections and bars states from issuing any mail ballot unless the voter submits a written or electronic request affirming eligibility under a narrow list of criteria such as active military service, age 65 or older, disability, or temporary absence from the county.

scores.thoughts: The bill contains no provisions related to federal, state, or local government budgets, appropriations, or expenditures. It solely regulates the distribution of mail ballots in federal elections.
The bill does not address tax rates, tax policy, deductions, credits, or revenue collection in any way.
No provisions in the bill relate to healthcare delivery, insurance, public coverage, or market-based reforms.
The bill has no connection to firearms regulation, gun rights, or Second Amendment issues.
Nothing in the bill addresses immigration pathways, border enforcement, visas, or immigrant protections.
The legislation contains no language concerning reproductive rights, abortion access, or related restrictions.

While the bill includes active-duty military members as one eligible category for mail ballots, this is a narrow exception within an election-integrity measure and does not alter military spending or defense policy.
The bill has no bearing on environmental regulations, climate policy, or conservation efforts.
No provisions affect welfare programs, food assistance, unemployment benefits, or other safety-net policies.
The bill does not address school funding, curriculum, school choice, or federal education policy.
The legislation is silent on drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance-abuse policy.
The bill mentions incarceration only as one narrow eligibility criterion for mail ballots and does not alter sentencing, policing, or rehabilitation policies.
No trade, tariff, or globalization provisions appear in the bill.
The bill does not address deficit spending, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
The legislation contains no language concerning LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
No provisions relate to foreign assistance, international aid, or diplomatic spending.

The bill directly regulates mail-in voting for federal elections by prohibiting unsolicited ballots and restricting eligibility to a narrow list of categories (military, students away from home, clergy, disabled voters, seniors 65+, etc.). This constitutes a clear election-integrity measure that limits broad access to mail ballots, aligning with the +1 end of the spectrum.
The bill does not address data privacy, technology regulation, or surveillance policy.
No provisions concern worker protections, union rights, or employer flexibility.
The bill does not engage with religious exemptions, civil-rights enforcement, or anti-discrimination law.
